title: RightNow AI Releases AutoKernel: An Open-Source Framework that Applies an Autonomous Agent Loop to GPU Kernel Optimization for Arbitrary PyTorch Models
author: Asif Razzaq
thesis: An autonomous LLM agent loop — write candidate kernel, benchmark, keep or revert, commit to git — can mechanize GPU kernel optimization across arbitrary PyTorch models, beating torch.compile on 12/16 H100 configurations and even outperforming hand-tuned CUTLASS on specific shapes. The expert kernel engineer's workflow is itself a simple loop, and agents can run it at 40 experiments/hour for 10+ hours without human intervention.
key_insights: Ralph Wiggum edit-benchmark-keep/revert loop mechanized with git-as-state-machine (commit = keep, git reset = revert, tab-separated results.tsv for logs)

5-stage correctness harness gates every speedup: smoke test, shape sweep (8-10 configs x FP16/BF16/FP32), adversarial numerical stability, 3x determinism check, non-power-of-two edges (1023/4097/1537)
Amdahl's-law target ranking via torch.profiler with shape recording — effort allocated by runtime share, not per-kernel benchmark

909-line program.md encodes 6-tier optimization playbook (block sizes -> memory access -> compute -> advanced -> architecture-specific -> kernel-specific algorithms) so agent runs 10+ hours without getting stuck
Orchestrator transitions when any of: 5 consecutive reverts / 90% GPU peak reached / 2hr elapsed / 2x speedup achieved
Each iteration = 90 seconds (30s correctness + 30s benchmark via Triton do_bench + 30s agent reasoning), 40 experiments/hour, 300-400 experiments per overnight 10hr run on 1 GPU
Direct intellectual transplant of Andrej Karpathy's autoresearch loop (which found 20 LLM training optimizations in 700 experiments over 2 days on 1 GPU)

benchmark_results.hardware: NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (132 SMs, CC 9.0, CUDA 12.8)
benchmark_results.rmsnorm: 5.29x over PyTorch eager, 2.83x over torch.compile (max-autotune), 2788 GB/s = 83% of 3352 GB/s HBM3 peak
benchmark_results.matmul_2048_cubed: 1.55x over torch.compile max-autotune (cuBLAS gap not yet closed)
benchmark_results.community_fp4_matmul: beats hand-tuned CUTLASS C++ by 1.63x-2.15x across shapes (single ~3min agent run)
benchmark_results.summary: Beats torch.compile on 12 of 16 representative configurations

correctness_harness_stages: Stage 1 — Smoke test: small input, catches compile errors and shape mismatches, <1s
Stage 2 — Shape sweep: 8-10 input configurations x 3 dtypes (FP16/BF16/FP32), catches size-dependent bugs (boundary handling, tile remainder)
Stage 3 — Adversarial numerical stability: large identical softmax rows, extreme matmul dynamic range, near-zero normalization variance
Stage 4 — Determinism: 3x bitwise-identical runs catches race conditions in parallel reductions and non-deterministic atomics
Stage 5 — Non-power-of-two edges: 1023, 4097, 1537 dimensions expose masking bugs and tile remainder errors
Dtype tolerances: FP16 atol=1e-2, BF16=2e-2, FP32=1e-4
Paper eval: 34/34 H100 configurations passed with 0 failures

backends.triton: Primary backend — Python-like DSL, JIT compiles in 1-5s, reaches 80-95% of cuBLAS matmul throughput, ideal for rapid agent iteration
backends.cuda_cpp: Secondary — for warp-level primitives, WMMA tensor core 16x16x16 fragments, float4/half2 vectorized loads, bank-conflict-free shared memory, double buffering
backends.unified_interface: Both expose kernel_fn(), benchmark infrastructure runs identically regardless of backend

hardware_support.unknown_gpus: Estimates peak FP16 throughput from SM count, clock rate, compute capability

file_architecture.results.tsv: Plain TSV experiment log — dependency-free, human-readable, agent-parseable

deep_dive_candidates.why: The AutoKernel paper itself — likely contains full 34-config H100 benchmark table, the 909-line program.md playbook, ablations, and the orchestrator state machine. Highly relevant for our harness design patterns.

Direct intellectual parent of AutoKernel; same keep/revert loop applied to LLM training code; 20 optimizations across 700 experiments in 2 days on 1 GPU. Closes the loop on Karpathy's broader body of work alongside his LLM Wiki and AgentHub posts already in our catalogue.

The 250-problem GPU kernel benchmark AutoKernel was designed to beat. Frontier LLMs match PyTorch baseline in <20% of cases one-shot. Useful reference for agent capability on systems-engineering tasks.
RightNow AI commercial IDE product. AutoKernel is their research release. Worth a tool-catalogue pass to understand commercial angle and how the research connects to their IDE offering.

why_this_matters: First clear demonstration that the Ralph Wiggum edit-benchmark-keep/revert loop generalizes from application code into systems engineering domains where human expertise takes years to develop. Validates the thesis that agents will eat every domain with a tight feedback loop. The 5-stage correctness harness is a concrete template we should steal for our E2E gate. The git-as-state-machine pattern (commit = keep, reset = revert) is exactly how we use worktrees — now with production benchmark results beating torch.compile and even hand-tuned CUTLASS on specific shapes.
